description: Implement flash package with view integration - flash messages from session shown in views
steps: Create src/stdlib_flash.c with: flash.set(type, message) to store a flash message (type is 'success', 'error', 'info', 'warning'), flash.get(type) to retrieve and clear flash of that type, flash.all() to get all flashes as a list of maps [{type: 'success', message: 'Saved!'}] and clear them. flash.has(type) returns bool. Use session.flash_set/flash_get internally (access the session's flash_data ObjMap directly via extern or through a shared internal interface).

Add a flash.render() function that outputs HTML for flash messages using the view builder. It should check if there's an active html builder (from stdlib_view.c) and if so, write styled flash message divs directly. Pattern:
{message}
for each pending flash message. This integrates flash with the view rendering system.
Add flash.render_inline() that returns the flash HTML as a string (using the render_inline pattern from stdlib_view.c - push a builder, write flash HTML, pop and return string).
Expose the builder_current() and builder_write() functions from stdlib_view.c so stdlib_flash.c can write to the active builder. Add appropriate extern declarations or a shared internal header.
Add init function declaration to src/vek_stdlib.h
Add package registration to src/vek_stdlib.c in stdlib_init() - flash package should be registered AFTER session package since it depends on session state
Create integration test tests/programs/stdlib_flash.ve + .expected testing flash.set, flash.get, flash.all, flash.has, and flash.render_inline
Run 'make clean && make' and 'make test' to verify everything passes
acceptance_criteria: make clean && make compiles without errors
flash.all() returns list of all flash maps and clears them
flash.has('success') returns true when set, false when not
flash.render_inline() returns HTML string with flash message divs
findings: Flash package implemented with independent global ObjMap state (not tied to session). Pre-existing test failures in stdlib_db and variables are flaky/unrelated (confirmed by stash test). The ObjMap iteration order is insertion order which makes render_inline output deterministic.
